title: Monthly Supply Rate Measure for C&I Termination Security
content:
## Termination security: measuring the monthly supply rate (Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts)

The termination security's monthly supply rate depends on how many billed cycles were posted on the contract in the twelve months before the handling date:

- **twelve or more cycles:** the twelve months' net charges (supply lines plus rebill credits posted in that window) divided by the cycles counted;
- **three to eleven cycles, at least one of them posted in the latest three months:** the net charges posted in the latest three months divided by the cycles posted in those three months;
- **any other count** (fewer than three cycles, or none posted in the latest three months): the net charges of the most recently posted cycle, meaning that cycle's supply lines plus any rebill credit dated to that cycle.

## Counting cycles

Each billed cycle is counted once: by its energy charge line; on a block and index contract, by its block energy charge line, the index energy charge lines then not being counted; or otherwise by its index energy charge line. Capacity and transmission charge lines never count a cycle.

## Windows and net charges

- A line falls in the twelve months before the handling date when it was posted on or before the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months have passed from its posted date to the handling date, a month being complete on the same day of the month as the posted date. With a handling date of 4 October 2026, a line posted on 4 October 2025 is outside the window and a line posted on 5 October 2025 is inside it.
- The latest three months are counted in the same way with three whole months.
- The net charges of a window are the amounts of the supply lines (energy, block energy, index energy, capacity and transmission charge lines) posted in it plus the rebill credits posted in it, the credits being negative amounts.
- The most recently posted cycle is the cycle of the supply line with the latest posted date; a rebill credit is dated to the cycle of the line it corrects.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Cycles in the twelve months | Cycles in the latest three months | Net charges used | Monthly supply rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 3 | twelve months, $516000.00 | 516000.00 divided by 12, $43000.00 |
| 7 | 2 | latest three months, $81400.00 | 81400.00 divided by 2, $40700.00 |
| 5 | 0 | most recently posted cycle, $38950.00 | $38950.00 |
| 2 | 2 | most recently posted cycle, $41120.00 | $41120.00 |
